Sean / Laura,

Thanks for the sync today. A quick follow-up from Procurement: the legal team flagged the holdback trigger in section 4.2 of the draft SOW — they want a concrete remediation cadence and a short list of mitigations that we (WellPath) can expect before they release the final 25% payment. Before we loop legal, can Redwood give us a proposed emergency MAP (short form) that commits to:

- a 5-business-day stabilization sprint for any acceptance failures;
- a single technical contact and daily stand cadence during the sprint;
- a fallback model variant that can be used if performance regresses beyond agreed thresholds.

If you can send that by EOD Monday, it will prevent a holdback rewrite on our side. We also need to see a high-level risk log for the last 30 days tied to acceptance tests.

Best,
Elise

Hi Elise — thanks, clear ask.

We can provide the short-form emergency MAP and a 30-day risk snapshot. Draft plan below, happy to formalize into a one‑page MAP_v3 and the XLS. High level:

Emergency MAP (summary)
- Trigger: any acceptance test failure >2% error rate or regression >5 p.p. in end-to-end accuracy over two consecutive daily windows.
- Response window: initial triage within 4 hours, mitigation plan within 24 hours, stabilization sprint (up to 5 business days).
- Cadence: daily stand (30m) + nightly status note to named PO.
- Fallback: automatic routing to v-quantized-1 (slightly lower throughput/cost) with traffic shift policy and manual rollback guard.

We will attach the MAP_v3 (one page) and a Risk-Log CSV with recent incidents. Proposed names for daily stand: Jared Holt (WellPath) + Laura Bennett (Redwood AM) + Ben Carter (Escalation lead) + Sean (exec sponsor).

I will send the formal files by EOD Monday (PST). Sending Ben into the thread to seed the risk log and action items.

—Sean

Elise — copying the risk snapshot below (abridged) and proposed containment steps. Full CSV attached.

Risk snapshot (30d)
- 2027-12-14: Regression in entity extraction on claims parser — ~3.1% failure spike — mitigated by prompt set rollback (T+1).
- 2027-12-26: Throughput variance during peak run — brief queue growth; autoscaler tweak applied (T+0.5).
- 2028-01-03: End-to-end eval drift vs baseline (4.7 p.p.) caused by prompt drift in test harness; running isolated canary with v-quantized-1.

Containment & sprint plan (if trigger fires)
Day 0 (Triage): 4h triage, capture logs, freeze model config.
Day 1: Hotfix candidate + nightly smoke tests; daily stand.
Day 2–4: Iterative remediation; deploy canary; monitor SLA windows.
Day 5: Stabilize and hand back with acceptance checklist.

Escalation ladder
- Ben Carter (technical escalation) — owner of remediation runs; public status reports to PV team.
- Laura Bennett (AM) — commercial and acceptance negotiation owner.
- Sean Gallagher — executive escalation and credit approvals.

Attachments: MAP_v3.pdf; Risk-Log-DW-9347.csv; WellPath-SLA-holdback-conditions.xlsx

Elise — following up with the short-form MAP (attached) and a suggested contract blurb for section 4.2 that legal can consider. Suggested clause (plain language):

"If Redwood fails an acceptance window as defined in Exhibit A, Redwood will initiate the Emergency MAP within 4 hours and undertake a stabilization sprint of up to five business days including named daily contacts, progress reports, and a documented remediation checklist. WellPath may withhold up to 25% of final payment pending the outcome of the MAP; Redwood will provide nightly evidence of remediation steps and may offer a credit if remediation extends beyond agreed windows."

Let us know if your legal team wants redlines; if not, we can accept that framing and move the SOW to signature.

Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Success | Redwood Inference
